chunks.arabic_text: وَرَوَى الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ الرَّقِّيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ:

translations.en: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: فِي الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ بَدَنَةٌ وَاجِبَةٌ فِي فِدَاءٍ

translations.en: Regarding a man upon whom a camel is obligatory as expiation.

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ «إِذَا لَمْ يَجِدْ فَسَبْعُ شِيَاهٍ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ صَامَ ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا، بِمَكَّةَ أَوْ فِي مَنْزِلِهِ

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: “If he does not find one, then seven sheep. If he is unable, he should fast eighteen days, in Mecca or in his home.”

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who owes a badanah as expiation in fidāʾ. If he cannot provide the camel, he substitutes it with seven sheep, and if he cannot afford that, he fasts eighteen days, whether in Mecca or at his place of residence.
en.seo_question: What must a muhrim do if a camel is obligatory as expiation but he cannot provide it?

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel due as a sacrificial expiation.
key_terms.فِدَاءٍ: Expiation or compensatory ransom for a violation.
key_terms.شِيَاهٍ: Sheep given as the substitute offering.
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا: Eighteen days of fasting as the final substitute.
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: In Mecca, where the fasting may be performed.
